newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates inch up in week.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates inch up in week.

text.p: Mortgage rates edged higher this week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.

Rates on 30-year, fixed-rate loans rose 7.87 percent on average from 7.85 percent last week while rates on 15-year loans edged up to 7.38 percent from 7.35 percent, the agency, known as Freddie Mac, said.
One-year adjustable-rate loans also rose, with the rate averaging 5.57 percent, up from 5.54 percent.
A year ago, 30-year loan rates averaged 7.02 percent, the 15-year rate stood at 6.53 percent, and one-year adjustable rate loans were 5.48 percent.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans and 1.4 percent on one-year adjustable loans, both unchanged from last week. They charged 1.7 percent on 15-year loans, down from 1.8 percent last week.
